key_insight: FERPO improves continuous-control policies by fitting the actor to an entropy-regularized target action distribution, avoiding unreliable critic action-gradients while encouraging broad exploration.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical on-policy RL update rule that can yield more stable actor learning and faster updates in robotics/control systems where value accuracy does not guarantee useful policy gradients.
method: Derive a target action distribution from a policy-improvement objective with entropy and KL regularization.
Fit the actor with a forward-KL objective estimated via self-normalized importance sampling from rollout actions.
Constrain the target to stay near the rollout policy so importance weights remain well behaved and multimodal coverage is preserved.
evidence_signal: The paper reports experiments and ablations on MuJoCo Playground and ManiSkill, showing competitive performance, sample-efficiency gains, and faster actor updates than REPPO.
watch_item: Forward-KL fitting depends on importance-sampling quality, so unstable weights or poor rollout coverage can hurt optimization if the KL constraint is too loose.
